Lately, I just can’t seem to turn my brain off. I’m an audit manager, so there’s always pressure, but even when I’m not at work, my mind races—about deadlines, my team missing targets, my wife’s job security, our mortgage, even worst-case scenarios like one of us getting seriously ill. It’s like one thought sparks another, and suddenly I’m spiraling into images of losing everything. I’ll be reviewing a report and catch myself worrying about my kid’s school performance, then jump to fearing a layoff, then imagine us not being able to afford health insurance. It’s constant. 

I know things have been stressful—my father’s been sick this past year, and we had some financial strain—but honestly, I was anxious way before that. Even when I got promoted two years ago, when nothing major was happening, I was still up at night worrying. It’s not that any one thing is wrong right now—it’s that my brain acts like something always is. I can’t relax, and it’s starting to affect my focus at work and time with my family.
D011-D020_h025.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
